subject: Request: Private endpoint egress evidence & firewall attestation
messages:
From: Tim Foster <tim.foster@acmehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Private endpoint egress evidence request

Hi Soojin / Laura,

We're starting our network and security sign-off for the Redwood private deployment in our staging VPC. The audit team has asked for a concise evidence packet so they can close the control. Concretely we need:

- Canonical list of IPv4/IPv6 addresses and CIDR ranges that Redwood control-plane and runtime will egress from (for allowlist and IDS rules). If there are per-region variants, please separate by region.
- A short description of which endpoints those IPs map to (control-plane API, telemetry, S3/backups, license attestation, health-checks).
- Attestation PDF signed by Redwood security stating these IPs are the only egress sources for the private endpoints and describing rotation policy (how often ephemeral IPs change).
- A diagram showing whether the egress is via a NAT gateway owned by Redwood, via a customer-managed proxy, or a hybrid (with expected TLS termination points).
- Any required ports/protocols (e.g., 443 outbound to api.redwood-inference.com) and SNI/CN fingerprints we should allow in our perimeter.

We have a hard deadline for the compliance pack on Jul 20 for our third-party audit. Can you confirm you'll provide the packet and whether you can provide a signed attestation (DocuSign) from Redwood Security? Also let me know if you need anything from our side (procurement contact, additional forms).

Thanks,
Tim
Tim Foster
Director, Platform Security
Acme Health

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Tim Foster <tim.foster@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress evidence request

Hi Tim — thanks for the clear list. We'll produce a consolidated evidence packet and a signed attestation for your audit. High-level plan below, delivered by Jul 16 EOD so you have a day to review before Jul 20: 

1) Evidence packet (attachments):
   - redwood-egress-ip-declaration.csv (columns: region, cidr, service, notes)
   - proxy-diagram-vpc.png (single-page diagram showing egress path and optional customer-managed proxy locations)
   - attestation-firewall-rules.pdf (formal signed statement from Redwood Security)

2) What we'll include in the CSV:
   - Control plane egress IPs (us-west-2 / eu-west-1 variants) and tokenized mapping to functional endpoints (e.g., control-plane.api.redwood-inference.com -> 34.125.88.0/26)
   - Runtime egress pool for non-sensitive telemetry (where applicable) and a note if that traffic is optional for your deployment
   - Rotation windows: ephemeral runtime egress IPs rotate on a 14-day rolling window by default; control-plane egress IPs for VPC/private endpoints are static per-region and not rotated except for maintenance with 2-week advance notice.

3) Attestation scope and signing:
   - The attestation will explicitly state: "To the best of Redwood Inference's knowledge as of the attestation date, the referenced IP addresses and ranges comprise the egress sources for the customer's private endpoints when configured with Redwood Private without customer-managed outbound proxies."
   - We'll include a clause listing exceptions (e.g., if the customer chooses to route outbound through their own proxy, Redwood cannot attest to customer-managed egress).

4) Questions for you:
   - Are you using a customer-managed outbound proxy (forward proxy) in front of the private connectors, or do you expect Redwood-managed NAT?
   - Do you need TLS fingerprinting for mutual TLS or just SNI allowlist entries?

I'll attach the initial CSV and diagram in the next email (working draft). If OK, Laura will provide the formal attestation PDF once we finalize wording.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Foster <tim.foster@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 17:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress evidence request

Hi Soojin / Laura,

Thanks for the quick reply and the proposed delivery date. A couple of clarifications from our audit team before you finalize the packet: 

- We need explicit confirmation whether TLS termination for control-plane API calls occurs at Redwood's edge (api.redwood-inference.com) or is tunneled through to a backend inside the private connector. If termination is at Redwood's edge, please provide the certificate CNs and the last 8 bytes of the cert fingerprint.
- For runtime telemetry/backups: are those writes made directly to third-party endpoints (S3, telemetry.redwood-inference.com) from within our VPC via outbound NAT, or do they traverse Redwood-managed egress nodes? Please state service-level mapping.
- Log retention for egress flows: we require that Redwood retain egress flow logs (source IP, dest IP, port, timestamp) for a minimum of 90 days for auditability. Can you confirm retention and whether logs are delivered or made available to us (S3 bucket or SIEM forward)?
- We will need a named contact on the procurement side for any DocuSign or contracting items related to the attestation.

Apologies for the detail — this is the standard evidence checklist. If you can add those clarifications to the packet that would be ideal.

Best,
Acme Health Security Team

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>, Tim Foster <tim.foster@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress evidence request

Tim / Acme Security — attaching the finalized evidence packet and attestation. See attachments listed below.

Summary responses to your clarifications:

- TLS termination: control-plane API TLS terminates at Redwood edge (api.redwood-inference.com). Certificate CNs: api.redwood-inference.com, controlplane-us.redwood-inference.com. Last 8 bytes of the current SHA256 cert fingerprints: a3:5f:9b:1c:4e:2d:7f:88 and 4c:2d:11:0a:9e:33:bb:cd (rotated certs documented in the attestation appendix).

- Runtime telemetry and backups: by default, runtime sends non-sensitive telemetry to telemetry.redwood-inference.com via Redwood-managed egress nodes unless the customer elects a customer-managed forward proxy. Backups that are configured to go to customer S3 buckets will egress from the customer-managed NAT/proxy and are not within Redwood's attestable IP set. The CSV maps each IP range to the service type.

- Log retention: Redwood retains egress flow logs (flow start, flow end, src ip, dst ip, dst port, protocol) for 180 days for Private customers by default. For customers requiring longer retention we can offer a configured export to an S3 bucket or Splunk/Datadog forward — details in page 3 of the packet.

- Procurement / DocuSign: please route contracting for the attestation to procurement@redwood.com. We'll assign an internal owner for the signature flow once we have your contact.

Attached (files):
- redwood-egress-ip-declaration.csv (CSV mapping: region,cidr,service,notes)
- proxy-diagram-vpc.png (diagram showing: customer VPC -> private connector -> optional customer-managed proxy or Redwood-managed NAT -> Redwood egress pool)
- attestation-firewall-rules.pdf (signed attestation; signature block: Laura Bennett, Head Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference)
